analysis:
The only change is in the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/MiMo/MiMoV26EncodedMediaIngressTests.swift, in testNativeMediaReleasePNGJPEGAndMP4GenerateThroughAuthenticatedRoutes (head ~343-347, ~380). It replaces a polling loop on managedMediaReservationCountForTesting with an event-driven wait. The new code uses an EventCounter, a testing hook setMediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting, and an expectation fulfilled after N removals. The final XCTAssertEqual(...ReservationCountForTesting, 0) is kept, so leaked-reservation detection is preserved. The test still covers the authenticated ingress, remote-URI refusal and media-reservation settlement paths. No production code, authorization, attestation, encryption, cache storage or wire-protocol code changed.

Remaining questions for integration:
- The hook setMediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting and the EventCounter helper are not visible in this batch, so I could not confirm they are test-only. If the hook is compiled into release builds, it would be a small new surface on the managed-media reservation lifecycle, but that is not evidenced here.
- Whether `removals.expectation(reaching:)` fires on exactly one removal per request, and not on other removals such as those from failed requests, is also not visible. That would only affect test reliability, not security.

No threat-model assets, trust boundaries or mitigations (T-041, TB-007 etc.) are affected. No regression identified.
